sample_unit: patients with large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy

links.outcome: ChatGPT thrombectomy decisions compared with board-certified stroke neurologists and neurointerventionalists on same patients
links.effect: ChatGPT agreed with the physician's decision whether or not to pursue thrombectomy in 54.3% of cases; mistakes in 8.8% of cases.
links.quote: ChatGPT agreed with the physician's decision whether or not to pursue thrombectomy in 54.3% of the cases.

links.outcome: Frequency of math, logic and misinterpretation errors in ChatGPT clinical reasoning outputs
links.effect: ChatGPT had mistakes in 8.8% of cases, consisting of mathematics, logic, and misinterpretation errors.
links.quote: ChatGPT had mistakes in 8.8% of the cases, consisting of mathematics, logic, and misinterpretation errors.

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating ChatGPT's clinical reasoning on real and simulated stroke thrombectomy cases compared to neurologist decisions, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
